title: InfoQ Launches High-Performing Teams Certification Program
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/high-performing-teams-program/en/headerimage/high-performance-teams-program-1790247868087.jpg"/><p>InfoQ has opened enrollment for a new five-week certification program covering engineering team design, delivery flow, AI-enabled work, and metrics, facilitated by InfoQ editor and podcast co-host Olimpiu Pop.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: Un-Mused: How a Single Debug Setting Bypassed macOS Security in Meta’s AI Client
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/meta-muse-zeroday/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790224330638.jpg"/><p>Security researcher Patrick Wardle revealed an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Meta's Muse desktop client for macOS. This flaw lets unprivileged software manipulate the assistant's extensive permissions, compromising input confidentiality and account security. Despite a hotfix from Meta, the vulnerability raises significant concerns about platform trust and security boundaries.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Building a Collaborative Platform Culture in a Bank
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/collaborative-platform-culture/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790072552423.jpg"/><p>A platform is a collaboration system, not infrastructure. Culture follows structure: platform teams can build open support sessions, create super user awards for contributing developers, and establish shared open standards to grow an engineering mindset. Developers and product teams depend on a platform team, which in turn depends on application teams; to go forward, they need shared standards.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: Designing Fast, Delightful UX With LLMs for Mobile Frontends
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/llm-mobile-frontend/en/mediumimage/bala-medium-1789631604448.jpeg"/><p>Balakrishnan Ramdoss discusses how to architect production-grade, AI-powered conversational apps at scale. He explains how to overcome model latency, leverage server-driven UI and Backend-for-Frontend patterns to dynamically render multi-modal interfaces, optimize prompts for UI selection, and integrate low-latency, privacy-first on-device AI for mobile applications.</p> <i>By Balakrishnan Ramdoss</i>

title: Canvas UI Ships 35 HTML-in-Canvas Components That Run WebGL and WebGPU Effects Over Live DOM
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/canvas-ui-webgl/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790080690608.jpg"/><p>Canvas UI is an open-source component library created by David Haz, utilizing the experimental HTML-in-Canvas API. It features 35 components that render GPU effects on live page content while maintaining accessibility. The library integrates with multiple frameworks and requires specific Chrome versions for full functionality.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Apple Reference Image Signs Photos at the Sensor, Moving Provenance Trust Away from C2PA
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Apple has published the design of Reference Image, an iPhone 18 Pro camera mode that signs pixel data at the sensor and develops it in Private Cloud Compute under an Apple signature. Developers on Hacker News and Reddit challenged what it proves, raising photographing a screen, the anonymity guarantee's dependence on Apple's cloud, and whether identity verification is the right use case.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Graphify: Unifying Codebase Context to Streamline Agentic Software Engineering
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Graphify is an open-source tool designed to convert codebases and unstructured data into queryable knowledge graphs. Launched in April 2026, it addresses challenges of multi-file reasoning for AI coding assistants. Recent updates have enhanced parser features and cross-file resolutions. Community feedback indicates a promising architecture but notes integration challenges in daily workflows.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Beyond Kubernetes at Modal: How to Scale 1 Million Concurrent Sandboxes in Seconds
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/modal-scaling-sandboxes/en/headerimage/agent-sandbox-kubernetes-1790170874561.jpeg"/><p>In a recent article, Colin Weld and Connor Adams, staff engineers at Modal, describe how they rebuilt their sandbox infrastructure from the ground up to support millions of concurrent sandboxes and tens of thousands of sandbox creations per second.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Cloudflare Cuts 100 TB of Memory from 1.1.1.1 DNS Cache
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/cloudflare-dns-cache/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788755192272.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare redesigned the in-memory representation of its Big Pineapple DNS cache, reducing the per-entry footprint by 56% and freeing roughly 100 TB of working-set memory across its fleet. The Rust-based changes also increased cache insertion throughput by 43% and reduced lookup latency by 19%, while enabling Cloudflare to increase cache capacity without additional memory.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: APIs for Agents: Rethinking API Programs in the MCP Era
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/mcp-calm-api-architecture/en/mediumimage/jim-gough-andreea-niculcea-medium-1789021410351.jpg"/><p>Jim Gough and Andreea Niculcea explain how Morgan Stanley uses Architecture as Code with CALM to modernize its API program. They demonstrate integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications, enforcing automated governance through deployment gates, and executing zero-downtime platform upgrades to safely scale enterprise AI and agentic workflows.</p> <i>By Jim Gough, Andreea Niculcea</i>

title: Andrew Kelley Interview: Why He Built Zig, Banned AI Contributions, and Moved Zig off GitHub
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/andrew-kelley-zig-no-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790159119456.jpg"/><p>In a JetBrains interview, Zig creator Andrew Kelley expanded on the project’s formal ban on AI contributions and the motivation behind its migration off GitHub to Codeberg: automated code submissions decrease codebase quality and weaken the social constructs between open-source participants; persistent GitHub failures and a perceived misalignment of incentives led to migrating to Codeberg.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: Google Adds Cycle-Level Kernel Profiling to XProf
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/google-tpu-xprof/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790149843663.jpg"/><p>Google has added a Kernel Profiling suite to XProf. This is its open-source profiler for TPU workloads. Now, developers can see cycle-level details in custom Pallas kernels. Before, these kernels appeared as single opaque blocks in trace captures.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Article: Modular Edge Computing at Multi-Tenant SaaS Scale on Cloudflare Workers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/modular-edge-computing/en/headerimage/modular-edge-computing-header-1789559793469.jpg"/><p>At multi-tenant SaaS scale, a monolithic edge worker creates deployment coupling and broad blast radius. The article presents a modular Cloudflare Workers architecture using service bindings, with image optimization as a worked example of per-tenant format negotiation and device-aware sizing. It covers multi-CDN differences, staged releases, configuration, and testing.</p> <i>By Chintan Tank</i>

title: Elastic Beanstalk Adds Cluster Mode, Running Applications on Shared EKS Clusters
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has added Cluster Mode to Elastic Beanstalk, running applications on EKS clusters the service creates and operates. Clusters are assigned by subnet set and cannot be changed afterward, direct cluster access is service-managed, and AWS recommends separate clusters for untrusted or regulated workloads. The mode adds EKS and Auto Mode fees that EC2 discounts do not reduce.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Google Open-Sources AX a Kubernetes Style Orchestrator for Autonomous AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/google-ax-orchestrator/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790059907704.jpg"/><p>Google has open-sourced AX, an orchestrator designed for managing autonomous AI agent workloads. AX operates on a runtime, Agent Substrate, treating agents as stateful actors. It provides resource-efficient task suspension and resumption to optimise performance and reduce latency in idle phases. It features a control plane with Kubernetes-style primitives for managing agent tasks and resources.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>
